resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection (City Code Section 55-13; formerly called the Residential Certificate of Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Gloucester City Buildings and Housing Office (Housing Inspector / Code Enforcement Official)
resale_co.valid_for: Until the next new occupant or transfer of title; not transferable
requirements: Home must comply with the applicable provisions of the City code (Housing Code, Chapter 55)

Smoke detectors certified by the Fire Official: hard-wired interconnected battery backup or 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms on or near the ceiling of each level, and battery smoke detectors in each bedroom or sleeping area
Owner supplies the address, owner name, address and phone, and the name and age of each person who will occupy the home
Warrant waiver from the Gloucester City Municipal Court (313 Monmouth Street) showing no outstanding warrants for the buyer, owner, tenants and proposed occupants
Violations must be fixed and reinspected within 90 days of the first report (one extension to 120 days if asked for in time), or a new application and fee are needed

fees.label: Initial inspection and first reinspection, residential
fees.quote: $100 for the initial inspection and first reinspection, if needed;

fees.label: Certificate for Transfer of Property Title (vacant property sale only; a Certificate of Inspection application must follow within 90 days)
fees.quote: The said fee for a Certificate of Transfer of Property Title is $75.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply to the Buildings and Housing Office, 700 Somerset Street, Gloucester City, NJ 08030 (856-456-7689, housing@cityofgloucester.org) with the City's certificate application, and get the warrant waiver from the Municipal Court at 313 Monmouth Street. The City website (cityofgloucester.org) is behind a bot check and could not be read this time, so the current application form and payment methods were not confirmed. A vacant property can instead be sold with a Certificate for Transfer of Property Title ($75, valid 90 days) if a Certificate of Inspection application is filed before it expires.
resale_co.contact_title: Director - Chief Housing Inspector & Zoning Official (as listed in April 2024)

evidence.quote: The Certificate for Transfer of Property Title is valid for 90 days
Inspect and issue Certificates of Occupancy. Issue violations of the Certificates of Occupancy (Code 55-13).

resale_co.notes: New this check: the current City code is now on ecode360 and was read in full. Section 55-13 (amended by Ord. No. O18-2024 on 7-22-2024 and Ord. No. O01-2025 on 2-24-2025) now calls the document a 'certificate of inspection' and requires the owner or agent to get one before any new occupant moves in and before title to improved property is transferred by purchase or otherwise. Fees are now quoted from the current code ($100 / $15 / $50 residential, $75 transfer certificate) instead of the 2019 archived form; the amounts did not change. The 90-day abatement window with one 120-day extension is in Sections 55-13G and H. Contact change: the City's April 2024 Housing page lists William Gallagher as Director - Chief Housing Inspector & Zoning Official (williamgallagher@cityofgloucester.org, 856-456-7689 x 405); the prior record named William Ackley from a 2020 page. The live site returns a Cloudflare bot check, so this could not be confirmed as current. Commercial certificates have separate square-foot fees. Section 55-14 rental registration and Section 55-14.1 lead-based paint inspections are rental programs, not resale requirements. A Zoning Certificate application is $50 (Section 55-12.1), but nothing ties it to a home sale.

requirements: Hard-wired interconnected battery backup smoke detectors or 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms on or near the ceiling of each level
Battery smoke detectors in each bedroom or sleeping area
Carbon monoxide alarm rules were not found in the City code section; ask the Housing Office

authorities.name: Gloucester City Fire Department Bureau of Fire Prevention (Fire Official Patrick R. Hagan), certifying smoke detectors for the Housing Office's Certificate of Inspection; DCA lists 'Gloucester City Housing' as the smoke detector compliance contact
authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke detector check is tied to the Housing Office's Certificate of Inspection: City Code 55-13 C(1) says the certificate is issued once the Fire Official or other authorized staff certify the smoke detectors, and the DCA directory lists Gloucester City Housing, (856) 456-7689, as the smoke detector compliance contact. No separate smoke/CO application or fee was found. Fire Official: Patrick R. Hagan, (856) 456-2652.

evidence.quote: a certificate of occupancy shall be issued by the Housing Inspector or Code Enforcement Official upon the certification by the Fire Official, or other duly authorized personnel, of the satisfactory installation of hard-wired interconnected battery backup smoke detectors or 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms
The local enforcement agency shall be the Bureau of Fire Prevention.
proper installation of smoke detectors in those structures shall be certified by the Fire Official, Inspector or other duly authorized personnel.
evidence.doc_date: City Code Chapter 48 (amended 4-3-2003 by Ord. No. 5a-2003)

evidence.quote: LEAID: 0414-001 Gloucester City SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Gloucester City Housing Enf Auth. Fire Dept Addr: 512 Monmouth St ... Fire Official Patrick R Hagan Phone (856) 456-7689 ... Phone (856) 456-2652 ... Email pat.hagan@gloucestercityfd.org

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA LEA registry (July 2026) lists Gloucester City as code F (Fire Department). City Code Chapter 48 names the Bureau of Fire Prevention as the local enforcing agency and ties smoke detector certification to Section 55-13(C). The DCA directory lists 'Gloucester City Housing' at 512 Monmouth St, (856) 456-7689, as the smoke detector compliance contact, so in practice the smoke check appears to happen with the Housing inspection. Chapter 48's fee table covers commercial registrations and permits, with no smoke/CO certificate fee. No official text with a separate $45 / $90 / $161 smoke certificate fee was found, so none is recorded. The code section does not mention carbon monoxide alarms or a fire extinguisher.

other_items.label: Municipal Court warrant waiver
other_items.detail: Get a warrant waiver from the Gloucester City Municipal Court, 313 Monmouth Street, for the buyer, owner, tenants and proposed occupants (City Code 55-13 D(4)).

other_items.label: Vacant property sale option
other_items.detail: A vacant structure can be transferred with a Certificate for Transfer of Property Title ($75, valid 90 days, one battery smoke detector per level inspected first), but a Certificate of Inspection application must be filed before it expires.

other_items.label: Outstanding Housing Office fees
other_items.detail: The City's 2019 application said that under Ordinance 019-2017 all fees owed to the Housing Office on the property, including vacant or abandoned property fees, must be paid before a certificate is issued. Not re-confirmed on a current City page.
